gaps.construct: parameter f of type func(int) bool, called inside the loop
gaps.description: The doc has no type for an operation value and no form for calling one held in a variable; 'an Operation from Int to Bool' and the call 'f h' are guesses.
No uses line means pure, but Go's f may have effects; the doc has no effect-polymorphic header ('uses whatever f uses'), so either every effectful f is rejected or the header lies.

gaps.construct: int(uint(i+j) >> 1) to compute the midpoint without overflow
gaps.description: No shift and no unsigned reinterpretation; replaced by i + (j - i) / 2, which is equivalent for 0 <= i <= j.

gaps.construct: invariants f(i-1) == false and f(j) == true with the virtual values f(-1) == false and f(n) == true
gaps.description: The doc has no way to define a value at a virtual index for spec purposes; written as 'i is 0 or not f (i - 1)', and calling a possibly impure f inside an invariant is not settled by the doc.

invented_syntax: given f is an Operation from Int to Bool
f h (calling a parameter as an operation)
not f (i - 1) (precedence of not over a call)
notes: The algorithm itself translates line for line, and the Go comment invariants become checkable invariant lines, which is a win. Everything hard is about the higher-order parameter: its type, its call syntax, and its effects. Every higher-order standard-library function (sort, search, filter with a predicate) will hit the same three gaps.
